decisions.reason: As an invested extension of the firm's specialty wafer technology, management is likely to continue A for now and explain weak traction as a temporary market-adoption or qualification issue.
B is a close, low-risk complement to the established wafer business and its public launch makes management inclined to stay committed rather than withdraw quickly.

C received a visible trade-fair launch and likely substantial development effort, so escalation of commitment makes management reluctant to abandon it while it can still blame results on long semiconductor design-in cycles.
Because D involved founding a new brand tied directly to the firm's core glass and quartz wafer offering, management has a strong public and strategic commitment to keep it in the market.
E appears more exploratory and less visibly committed than the wafer-focused launches, so despite sunk costs management is somewhat more likely to cut it and redeploy resources.
